findings.evidence:
`pkg/planner/cascades/memo/memo.go:258` iterates `src.hash2ParentGroupExpr.Each(...)` and, inside the callback, calls `mm.replaceGEChild(val, src, dst)`.
`pkg/planner/cascades/memo/memo.go:303` `replaceGEChild` calls `older.removeParentGEs(ge)` -> `pkg/planner/cascades/memo/group.go:220` which does `src.hash2ParentGroupExpr.Remove(...)` on the same map being iterated.
`go.mod:121` pins `github.com/zyedidia/generic v1.2.1`; in that implementation `hashmap.Map.Each` ranges over `m.entries` (`.../github.com/zyedidia/generic@v1.2.1/hashmap/map.go:203`) while `Remove` can rehash/move subsequent entries via `m.Put(...)` (`map.go:158-165`). This can move unvisited entries into earlier slots already passed by the range, so some parent GEs can be skipped and never updated.
`pkg/planner/cascades/memo/group.go:327` hashes parent refs by raw pointer value (`uint64(uintptr(t))`), while the hashmap uses low bits for the starting slot (`.../hashmap/map.go:62`), increasing clustering risk and making the skip more likely in practice.
findings.fix: Avoid mutating `src.hash2ParentGroupExpr` during iteration: first snapshot all parent GEs into a slice (via `Each`), then iterate that slice to run the update/removal logic. Optionally also change the pointer hash to a mixed hash (e.g., xor-shift/murmur) to reduce clustering, but the correctness fix is to not `Remove` from the map being iterated.
findings.impact: Some parent `GroupExpression`s may keep `src` in `Inputs` after `src` is removed/cleared, producing a memo graph with dangling child pointers. This can lead to planner panics (nil logical props / empty groups) or incorrect/missing exploration results (wrong plan enumeration / skipped transforms) under cascades.
findings.later_fix_evidence: Checked `upstream/master` at `3b531d4e3d99cb988bebccb8f63a96afff0ec6cd`: `pkg/planner/cascades/memo/memo.go` still iterates `src.hash2ParentGroupExpr.Each(...)` and `replaceGEChild` still removes from the same map; `go.mod` still uses `github.com/zyedidia/generic v1.2.1`.
findings.verify: Add a regression test where a group with multiple parent GEs is merged, and assert every former parent GE’s `Inputs` no longer reference `src` and `src.hash2ParentGroupExpr.Size()==0` afterward. Run `go test ./pkg/planner/cascades/memo -run TestMergeGroup` (plus the new case).
findings.what: `Memo.mergeGroup` mutates `src.hash2ParentGroupExpr` while iterating it, so some parent GEs can be skipped and never updated to point from `src` to `dst`.

findings.evidence:
`pkg/planner/cascades/memo/group.go:208` `ForEachGE` advances with `elem = elem.Next()` and does not prefetch `next` before calling the callback.
`pkg/planner/cascades/memo/group.go:235` `Group.mergeTo` calls `g.ForEachGE(...)` and in the duplicate case calls `ge.mergeTo(existedGE)` (`group.go:249`).
`pkg/planner/cascades/memo/group_expr.go:151` `GroupExpression.mergeTo` calls `e.GetGroup().Delete(e)`, which removes the current list element from `Group.logicalExpressions`.
Go stdlib confirms removal breaks `Next()` traversal: `/Users/bba/.gvm/gos/go1.25.1/src/container/list/list.go:107` sets `e.next=nil` and `e.list=nil` on removal; `(*Element).Next()` returns nil when `e.list==nil` (`list.go:30-36`). So once a duplicate GE is deleted during iteration, `elem.Next()` becomes nil and `ForEachGE` stops early, leaving the remaining src GEs unprocessed before `g.Clear()`.
findings.fix: Make `Group.mergeTo` iterate safely when deletions can occur: use a manual loop that stores `nextElem := elem.Next()` before any operation that might delete the current element, or first snapshot the GEs into a slice and iterate that slice. Avoid using `ForEachGE` here unless it is made deletion-safe by design.
findings.impact: When merging groups with duplicates and multiple source GEs, only a prefix of `src` GEs get migrated/merged; remaining GEs can be lost from the memo traversal while still present in `mm.hash2GlobalGroupExpr` or task stacks. This can cause planner panics (stale `GE.group` pointing to a cleared/removed group) and/or missed logical alternatives, leading to incorrect optimization behavior (potentially wrong plan choice or failure to find a feasible/best plan).
findings.later_fix_evidence: Checked `upstream/master` at `3b531d4e3d99cb988bebccb8f63a96afff0ec6cd`: `pkg/planner/cascades/memo/group.go` still has the same `ForEachGE` and `Group.mergeTo` calling `ge.mergeTo` inside it; `pkg/planner/cascades/memo/group_expr.go` still deletes the GE from the group in `mergeTo`.
findings.verify: Add a regression test where `src` has multiple GEs and at least one is equivalent to a GE in `dst`, then merge and assert all non-duplicate src GEs are present in `dst` afterward and no `mm.hash2GlobalGroupExpr` entry points to a cleared/removed group. Run `go test ./pkg/planner/cascades/memo -run TestRecursiveMergeGroup` (plus the new case).
findings.what: `Group.mergeTo` can stop iteration early because it deletes the current list element while iterating, so not all source `GroupExpression`s are migrated/merged before the source group is cleared.

subject: planner: add memo group merge logic. (#58470)
summary: Reviewed commit 432110b9 (PR #58470) diff vs parent, focusing on `pkg/planner/cascades/memo`. Found two High-severity correctness hazards in the new group-merge implementation: (1) mutating `hash2ParentGroupExpr` while iterating it can skip parent updates, leaving dangling child-group pointers; (2) deleting list elements during `ForEachGE` traversal can terminate merge iteration early, leaving orphan/unmerged GEs. Both issues still exist on `upstream/master` as of 3b531d4e3d99 (not fixed later).
